subject: Kickoff: BYO-key inventory & emergency evacuation playbook for Acme private deployment
messages:
From: Tom Harris <t.harris@acme-corp.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Cc: security@acme-corp.com, ops-aws@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 29 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kickoff: BYO-key inventory & emergency evacuation for Acme private deployment

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting the security onboarding for the Acme private deployment (VPC + hybrid on-prem connectors). Two immediate asks from our side:

1) Inventory template: we need a canonical inventory of all key material that will be present in our environment (HSM-backed KEKs, wrapped model keys, service-account wrapping keys, operator keys, backup archives). Can you send a template that your ops team prefers?

2) Emergency evacuation / operator eviction playbook: given our compliance constraints, we need a documented runbook that covers the steps to: isolate the tenant, zeroize any operator-accessible secret material, rotate customer KEKs, and provide audit evidence within a 72-hour SLT.

A few constraints to keep in mind:
- We plan to use AWS CloudHSM (nCipher alternative later) for the customer KEK.
- No plaintext customer master keys may exist outside the HSM boundary.
- Egress controls: we cannot allow any key material to be exported to third-party control planes without an escrow and signed attestation.

I've attached the initial questionnaire and our compliance team's checklist. Can we schedule a 60-minute workshop next week to walk the inventory and agree the evacuation SLA? Ideally we want a dry-run before pilot.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Harris
Head of Cloud Security – Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_byo_questionnaire.xlsx
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
To: Tom Harris <t.harris@acme-corp.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.example.com, michael_grant@redwood.example.com, laura_bennett@redwood.example.com
Date: Tue, 29 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BYO-key inventory & emergency evacuation for Acme private deployment

Tom —

Appreciate the clear constraints. I've sketched an initial approach and attached two artifacts: a lightweight inventory template (neha_byo_inventory_template.xlsx) and a draft evacuation playbook (evac_playbook_draft_v1.pdf). High-level summary of the proposed model below.

Summary of proposed BYO-K flow (hybrid, audit-friendly):

- Customer KEK stays in customer-controlled HSM (CloudHSM). Redwood will never hold an unwrapped customer KEK.
- For runtime, we use a double-wrap pattern: model/service keys (DEKs) are encrypted with a Redwood ephemeral wrapping key, which is itself wrapped by the customer KEK in their HSM. The key ladder prevents plaintext keys leaving the customer's boundary.
- Ephemeral wrapping keys are short lived (default 12 hours) and rotated automatically by our runtime; we can shorten to 4 hours for the high-sensitivity pilot.
- Operator separation: operator service accounts do not possess KEK unwrap capability. We maintain an attested unwrapping proxy that performs unwrap operations only under strict RBAC and hardware attestations.
- Emergency evacuation procedure (short):
  1) Quarantine tenant network (block outbound to anything but Redwoods's attested endpoints and your ops endpoints).
  2) Revoke operator proxy certificates and rotate Redwood ephemeral wrapping keys.
  3) Request you to perform a HSM key rotation / rewrap in your CloudHSM (we provide the signed rewrap payload and verification steps).
  4) Run integrity checks and provide consolidated audit bundle (signed manifests, TLS session logs, attestation statements).

Audit evidence and retention:
- We produce signed manifests for each unwrap/rewrap operation (RFC-compliant signatures), plus keystroke for operator actions and an append-only audit ledger. Default retention is 1 year; we can mirror to your S3 for longer durations.

Open questions for the workshop:
- Which CloudHSM model/firmware are you on (v2.x or v3.x)? That determines available mechanisms for external wrapping.
- Do you require offline key escrow (split custody) as a fallback for disaster recovery?
- Target evacuation SLA — you suggested 72 hours; we can commit to a 48-hour evidence delivery and a 96-hour full rotation if you need staged deadlines.

Next steps / proposed schedule:
- 60-minute workshop: Thu 2028-08-31 10:00–11:00 PT (engineers + security). Confirm attendees and we'll send a calendar invite.
- Action: I'll circulate the inventory template and a shorter one-page operator eviction checklist for your security ops to validate.

For visibility: cc'ing Stephanie (product security), Hannah (private deployment PM), Michael (runtime infra) and Laura (dedicated accounts lead).

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: neha_byo_inventory_template.xlsx, evac_playbook_draft_v1.pdf
From: Tom Harris <t.harris@acme-corp.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com, ops-aws@acme-corp.com
Date: Wed, 30 Aug 2028 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: BYO-key inventory & emergency evacuation for Acme private deployment

Neha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. A few clarifying items before the workshop:

1) Rotation cryptoperiod: our policy is max 90 days for KEKs; for DEKs associated with critical assets we require emergency rotation within 4 hours. Can Redwood support a 4-hour forced-rotation path and a fast rewrap that guarantees replayable audit evidence?

2) Audit bundles: we need the evidence to include the full unwrap/rewrap chain plus TLS session captures for the calls involved in rewrapping. Is that supported out-of-the-box or does it require extra agent deployment on our side?

3) Zero-knowledge assurance: we won't accept a model where any plaintext DEK exists in Redwood control plane memory unless it's within an attested enclave with verifiable measurement. Is the ephemeral wrapping done inside an attested enclave (e.g., Nitro enclave or similar) or in an application process?

4) Operator eviction dry-run: can you outline a 1-page on-call playbook for operator eviction (step-by-step) that we can run during the dry-run? We'll need to run the dry-run with our security ops in the first week after the pilot spin-up.

If you can address 1–3 in the workshop, we'll bring a CloudHSM engineer to confirm firmware compatibility.

Regards,
Tom

(Attached: updated Acme checklist — minor edits)
